title: Consumer-directed care can create flexible paid work while leaving unpaid carryover, training, benefits, and retention risks open
source_unit: ASPE Experiences of Workers Hired Under Cash and Counseling paid-worker follow-up
geography: United States; Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey Medicaid demonstration

observations.period: Cash and Counseling paid-worker follow-up; approximately nine to ten months after assignment, report published 2005

denominator.unit: directly hired workers under consumer direction compared with agency workers; state and adult/child outcome universes vary

work_route.value: Medicaid beneficiaries directly hired workers, often family members or friends, rather than relying only on agency workers

worker_satisfaction.value: directly hired workers were generally satisfied with working conditions, supervision, and compensation; more than 40% were very satisfied with wages and fringe benefits

unpaid_care_carryover.value: many directly hired workers continued substantial unpaid care

training_and_benefits.value: directly hired workers often had less formal training or benefits than agency workers, while generally feeling prepared

durability.unit: missing worker identity, beneficiary linkage, long-run retention, replacement worker, household income, later wage path, collective voice, and exit

mechanism.value: Flexible direct-hire care can convert some unpaid family/friend work into paid work while transferring hiring, supervision, payroll, and continuity risk into the beneficiary-worker household relationship

observations.method: Structured extraction from the ASPE report Experiences of Workers Hired Under Cash and Counseling; direct-hire and agency-worker comparisons, satisfaction, wages/benefits, training, unpaid carryover, and preparedness are kept separate from long-run retention and adequacy.
observations.uncertainty: Worker and agency comparison universes are study-specific, and direct-hire workers are often relatives or friends who previously provided unpaid care. The report does not establish individual wage adequacy, payment regularity, paid/unpaid hours, household security, or later wage path.
observations.subgroup: Directly hired and agency care workers serving Medicaid beneficiaries in Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey; no pooled worker-beneficiary household denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Worker satisfaction with a flexible paid role can coexist with modest wages, limited benefits, unpaid care, emotional or physical strain, and uncertainty about continuing.

boundary: This record establishes the paid-worker/provider side of consumer-directed Medicaid care. It does not establish adequate pay, completed care, long-run retention, beneficiary continuity, household recovery, collective voice, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the published ASPE worker report; worker, beneficiary, payroll, and Medicaid microdata are not retained.
